name: The Duel in the Hall
setup: You have been challenged in the Hall of Mirrors, which means you have been challenged by someone who may not be standing where you can see them, using a face that may not be theirs.

opponent.name: a Veilwright
opponent._poolsDerived_20260905: health removed: it was on the retired 3-7 scale and overrode a live synthesised sheet, which made a bout end in a median of ONE turn. The pool now derives from standing (30 + 5/level) through the level the threat implies. `yieldAtFraction` replaces an absolute `yieldAt` because a ratio is scale-free.

party.ifYouBringPeople: ⚠️ MORE OF YOU IS MORE FACES TO WEAR. The Veilwright will appear as a party member — ⛔ AND THE CELL'S BEST MOMENT IS A PARTY STRIKING ONE OF ITS OWN. ⚑ It lets you hit the wrong one; with three of you it lets you hit each other.
party.whatItAsksOfAParty: ⛔ Whether you can tell each other apart under pressure. ⚑ Knowing your people is the counter, and it is not a roll.
party.foldNote: ⚠️ A folded KNOW ally is the only reliable answer — someone whose whole job is watching which one is which.

_partyClauseWhy: ⛔ THE PARTY CLAUSE — R36/R36a, authored 2026-09-05. Every encounter in the corpus was written when a fight was ONE PERSON AGAINST ONE OPPONENT. ⚑ R36 makes a party member fight from their own sheet; R36a caps three acting fully and folds the rest. ⚠️ THE CLAUSE IS ADDITIVE — no prose changed. It is what a GM reads when more than one person is present.
